content.text:
The answer is Cs3DyO3 (mp-779546) alone, though the fit is not clean, so I can't fully rule out a second phase.

- **Single-phase fits:** Cs3DyO3 fits much better than the others tried, with an R-factor of 0.646. BaPr2CuO5, LuTaO4 and Sm2ZnPtO6 all stay near 0.96–0.97 and leave the main peak near 29° unexplained. I did not try VAg3O4, KAuO2, BaNaGdWO6, AgPdO2 or Li2MnFeO4 on their own; I only paired each with Cs3DyO3.
- **Two-phase fits:** adding any of those five to Cs3DyO3 barely helps. The best pairing, with KAuO2, lowers R only from 0.646 to 0.626. It does so by creating negative dips near 14.5° and 22°, which means it is fitting noise rather than real peaks.
- **What remains unexplained:** the leftover pattern still has structure. There is an unfitted peak near 16.2°, an extra peak near 30.8°, and a paired positive/negative feature at about 29–30°. That pair looks like Cs3DyO3's peak positions being slightly off rather than a separate phase. None of the other candidates accounts for these features, but they are why my confidence is moderate.
